title: cache-hf keys have one write job each; restore-only consumers set cache-mode read, not a restore-only input
answers: Windows HF datasets redownloaded every run after cache change
cache-hf restore-only input removed, how do I make a job read-only
which job writes the Linux or Windows hf-datasets cache
cache never refreshes after the cache-mode change
body:
Invariant: each cache key built by .github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml (`${{ runner.os }}-hf-datasets-<hash of tests/data/test_huggingface_dataset_and_source.py>`) must keep a job with `cache-mode: write`; consumers that only restore set `cache-mode: read` and pass no save-related input.
The composite no longer has a `restore-only` input or a separate actions/cache/restore branch; save is denied at token level by the job's cache-mode, so the grant is what changes saving.
The key includes runner.os, so the Linux writer (master.yml) and the Windows writer (the windows job in slow-tests.yml) are distinct; making the Windows job read leaves its key with no writer and every run redownloads datasets.
Fix pattern when adding an HF-cache consumer: set `cache-mode: read` on the job and do not add `restore-only`; add a write job only when a new runner.os key is needed.
Constraints: the writer-per-key list comes from review discussion on this PR and was not re-verified against every workflow; re-check the cache key before changing any writer grant.
applies: Jobs that call .github/actions/cache-hf and the cache-mode grants of the workflows that use it; not other caches.
says: Windows automated test runs are redownloading large dataset files on every build execution.
Dataset caches are never created or updated after switching build permissions to read-only.
Ensure continuous integration pipelines have a designated writing job for each operating system.
Build jobs fail when attempting to pass obsolete restore parameters into dataset caching.
search: Each cache key in .github/actions/cache-hf/action.yml requires exactly one workflow job configured with cache-mode: write, while restore-only consumers set cache-mode: read. Because the composite action removed the restore-only input and enforces saving at the token level, consumers must not pass save-related inputs. The Linux writer runs in .github/workflows/master.yml and the Windows writer runs in the windows job in .github/workflows/slow-tests.yml. Setting a platform writer to cache-mode: read leaves its runner.os key without a writer, forcing runs on that OS to redownload datasets every time.
